column1: # duty-cycle-registry.tsv — the OPT-IN list of roles the freeze-watchdog watches (Exec's design, 2026-06-16).
# A row = "watch this role." No row = not watched (not opted in / not migrated). To watch a new role, add a
# row; that's the whole registration step (no per-fire skill mutation).
# ⚠️ NEVER edit this file by round-tripping it through Python's `csv` module (csv.reader/csv.writer),
# even for a single-row edit. Root-caused 2026-09-23 (Docs, after two same-shape recurrences in 24h):
# this file mixes free-text prose (many agents type things like `"was:"` with plain quote marks) with
# real tab-delimited data, and has never been well-formed CSV/TSV. `csv.writer`'s default QUOTE_MINIMAL
# independently re-decides quoting for EVERY row based on whether that row happens to contain a literal
# `"` — unrelated to which row you meant to touch — silently wrapping+escaping prose fields and header
# comments nobody asked to change. SAFE PATTERN: locate your target by its `role\t` prefix (or a unique
# fragment) and replace only that line, everything else written back byte-for-byte unchanged —
# `scripts/trim-registry-history.py` already does this correctly; copy its approach, not the csv module.
# Both belt scripts (`duty-cycle-freeze-check.sh`, `cohort-freeze-detect.sh`) now detect and warn on the
# corruption signature (two consecutive double-quote characters, back to back) every time they run, so a
# recurrence surfaces on the next fire rather than waiting for someone to notice by chance — but that's a
# detector, not a preventer. (Corrected 2026-09-23, Docs: the ORIGINAL wording of this line typed the
# literal signature it was warning about, which made the detector flag this line itself — a permanent
# self-triggering false positive on every fire until fixed. Describe the pattern in prose; never spell
# it out literally in this file again.)
# "Actively cycling right now" is DERIVED from the session-log lifecycle the agent already maintains (m-36):
#   • session log carries  <!-- DAY-CLOSED -->            → cleanly STOPped today → not checked.
#   • no session log today AND before first_fire (+grace) → legitimately not STARTed yet → not checked
#       (kills the morning false-positive).
#   • no session log today AND PAST first_fire (+grace)   → SHOULD be cycling → CHECK heartbeat age. This is
#       the closed→never-restarted catch (Exec 2026-06-17): a role that cleanly STOPped + went dormant
#       overnight + missed its morning START shows a stale heartbeat past first_fire → flagged. (Without this
#       it read as "just hasn't started yet" and the load-bearing overnight-dormancy Gap-C slipped through.)
#   • else (STARTed, not yet STOPped)                     → CHECK heartbeat age vs threshold.
# ⚠️ CORRECTED 2026-07-27 (HOST found it; CIO owns both surfaces). This line USED to read:
#   "A live cycle commits every fire (push-to-main-routinely), so age > threshold_h here = genuinely frozen."
# That premise is FALSE and contradicted duty-cycle-tick SKILL.md, which tells agents the opposite:
#   "Batch identical daytime no-op holds (don't commit a near-duplicate entry each fire)" and
#   "Trivial/quiet-hold fires don't need an entry."
# So a CORRECTLY-EXECUTED quiet fire writes neither a commit nor a session-log line and is invisible
# to this watchdog BY CONSTRUCTION. The more faithfully an agent follows the no-churn discipline, the
# more often it is flagged frozen — we were alerting on COMPLIANCE. lead was alerted 3x on 07-27 while
# demonstrably alive and working. Measured across every row: ONE quiet fire trips ALL of them.
# INTERIM: thresholds widened to 2x(max inter-fire gap)+1h, which absorbs one quiet fire.
# ⚠️ This does NOT scale and is not the fix. Widening trades false positives for detection latency,
# and for low-frequency shapes the trade is bad: exec fires 2x/day, so 2x+1 = 25h — a dead exec
# unnoticed for a day. exec is therefore LEFT at 13h and remains exposed to a single quiet fire.
# The real defect is the INFERENCE, not the parameter: liveness is being derived from WORK OUTPUT,
# and work is legitimately bursty. The structural fix is a cheap per-fire heartbeat decoupled from
# work (one machine-readable line, not a prose log entry — which is what the skill actually forbids).
# Proposed to the cohort 2026-07-27; until it lands, treat a single STALE line on a 2x/day role as
# weak evidence and confirm before acting.
# ⚠️ WHAT THE CRON ACTUALLY IS — undocumented until 2026-07-31 (PA determined it by elimination).
# The duty cycle runs on the harness's **session-scoped `CronCreate`** tool. NOT the user crontab
# (that holds only Pard's freeze-watchdog), NOT launchd (no agent jobs there). This matters because
# `CronCreate` has TWO SILENT DEATH MODES:
#   1. SESSION-ONLY — the job dies when the Claude session exits. Every new session must re-arm.
#   2. 7-DAY AUTO-EXPIRY — announced once at creation and nowhere else.
# **Neither death emits anything. Both look exactly like a quiet day.**
# ⚠️ AND THE CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS FILE: `cron_expr` below records INTENDED CADENCE, NOT A LIVE JOB.
# A row can read `watched` with a plausible expression while no job exists at all — the registry
# cannot tell the difference, and neither can the freeze-watchdog that reads it. That is m-44 in the
# registry itself: the column looks identical whether the cron is armed, expired, or never created.
# **Only the owning agent can check** — `CronList` is session-scoped, so no other role and no script
# can verify your job is alive. Therefore: **state your JOB ID and its expiry date in your state
# column when you arm**, and re-verify at every START. Several rows already do this (arch, comms,
# docs); it is the only thing that makes an armed claim falsifiable by a reader.
# threshold_h = a bit more than the role's LARGEST in-window inter-fire gap (so a healthy role never trips).
# wake_start/wake_end = waking/alerting window (local hour, [start,end)); we don't alert PM outside it.
# first_fire = the role's first START-fire of the day, HH:MM (the first cron fire at/after wake_start — NOT an
#   overnight WATCH fire below wake_start). The "should be cycling by now" gate for the closed→never-restarted
#   catch. cio fires 03:07 (overnight WATCH, < wake_start 7) then 10:07 (START) → first_fire = 10:07.
# active_since = when the role joined the watch list (bookkeeping only).
# Columns (TAB-separated): role<TAB>cron_expr<TAB>threshold_h<TAB>wake_start<TAB>wake_end<TAB>first_fire<TAB>active_since[<TAB>state]
# state (col 8, OPTIONAL — absent/empty means `watched`, so every pre-2026-07-26 row is unchanged):
#   watched            → normal liveness checking (the default).
#   parked[: reason]   → deliberately dark. NO stall alerts, but STILL COUNTED: `DUTY_CYCLE_COVERAGE=1
#                        scripts/duty-cycle-freeze-check.sh` lists it as PARKED. Use this instead of
#                        commenting a row out — a commented row is skipped by the parser entirely and
#                        the role becomes structurally invisible (finding #6). An agent that comes back
#                        up overwrites its own row at START (duty-cycle-tick v1.17), clearing `parked`.
role
# ── ROSTER NOTE (CIO 2026-07-25, Exec-endorsed). The RUN-LEAN THROTTLE block that stood here expired
#    Wed Jul-1 and sat stale for three weeks; cleared. Current rows reflect actual live cadences.
#    ⚠️ COVERAGE IS NOT THE ROSTER (finding #6): this is an OPT-IN list, so a role with no row is
#    structurally invisible to the freeze-watchdog — it cannot be reported stale, only silently missed.
#    Five roles were dark six days while only `arch` alerted, purely because arch was the only one
#    registered: noise where there's coverage, silence where there isn't. Cure is upstream — each agent
#    writes its OWN row at START (duty-cycle-tick v1.17), because the load-bearing field is the cron
#    expression and that isn't knowable until the agent arms it. Do NOT add rows for dormant roles by
#    hand: that converts silence into repeating alerts about deliberately-parked agents and trains
#    everyone to ignore the belt. Any coverage claim from this file must state its denominator.
cio
